Order
23.03.2023 Order No.
01. 1.
None appears for the informant when the matter is called.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

3. The petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Case No.1817 of 2018, pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., COG-II, Bhubaneswar, arising out of Chandrasekharpur P.S. Case No.173 of 2018 for commission of alleged offences under Sections 403/406/420/120-B/34 of IPC.
4.

Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned 5th Additional District Judge, Bhubaneswar, by order dated 23.02.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he does not want to press the I.A. No.344 of 2023.
6. Accordingly, the I.A. No.344 of 2023 stands disposed of as not pressed.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner filed the legible copy of the FIR in Court.
The same is taken on record.

8. It is stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the case arises out of complaint case filed by the complainant-Bank on account of non-payment of hypothecation dues in respect of TATA LPK Santosh Prasad Mishra vs State Of Odisha ....

entities.text: TATA LPK Santosh Prasad Mishra vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154641736/
1 Tipper Vehicle.
9.
It is submitted that as the petitioner is in custody since 14.02.2023 and investigation has progressed substantially, he may be released on bail.
10. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.

11. It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that even if the entire allegation of the petitioner is taken at its face value, no criminal case under Section 420 of IPC and other allied sections is made out.

12. On consideration of materials on record, this Court finds sufficient force in the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that his further continuance of the petitioner in custody is punitive.

13. Taking into account the nature of accusation and keeping in view the guidelines, as fixed by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation & another,
reported in 2021 (10) SCC 773, this Court directs the petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.
